heroHeadline: NUG Rejects ASEAN Normalization of Junta; PDF Kills Pyu Saw Htee in Bago; 1,000+ Displaced in Hpruso; 72 Civilian Casualties in Myingyan District
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,926 of Myanmar's civil war (May 12, 2026), the National Unity Government formally condemned ASEAN's decision to hold virtual talks with the junta-installed foreign minister, calling it 'deeply contradictory' for military leaders who destroyed the 2020 election to demand international recognition — a rejection framed against the backdrop of the just-concluded ASEAN 46th Summit in Kuala Lumpur. In Bago Region, PDF forces killed two Pyu Saw Htee pro-military militia members and injured six in Okpho Township, with a separate resistance checkpoint attack in Letpadan, demonstrating sustained PDF pressure across the junta's critical logistics corridor between Yangon and Naypyidaw. A severe humanitarian crisis unfolded in Hpruso Township (Karenni State), where over 1,000 internally displaced civilians lack food and shelter after junta troops raided and burned villages, shot one man dead, and tortured another. In Myingyan District (Mandalay Region), a cumulative tally of 72 civilians killed or injured across four townships from SAC airstrikes, artillery, and ground operations underscored the relentless pace of junta violence — compounded by heatstroke deaths among displaced civilians unable to access shelter during extreme hot-season temperatures.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, Aryan Age, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
